name: Dina Hooper
episode: The missing name on the stern
life: “I still remember finding a stencil that hadn't been turned over in decades.” People around Breakwater Way know Dina by a small Thursday habit. Dina stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I kept the original stencil on the back of a cupboard door. We have been repainting a stranger's mistake for twenty years.
appearance: Dina is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Dina grins on one side while the eyes stay serious when listening.
personality: Dina has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Dina knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To bring the original stencil to the dock.
family: Una Vida is Dina’s half-sibling. Dina sets the time to leave. Una picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *An unfinished atlas*, Una says, “One of my students can read the tiny block letters upside down.”
connections: Rain Scott. A stencil and a set of removed letters are welcome in two different shore workshops.

reactions.situation: A family elder asks for the spelling they grew up with
reactions.response: Dina writes both spellings where the elder can indicate the one they prefer.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Dina keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Dina asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
